author: agent-sh
title: agent-sh/consult: cross-model second opinions inside coding-agent sessions
summary: A small open-source plugin lets a coding-agent session query another installed AI CLI in the background and return the answer inline. It supports read-only execution, reasoning-effort selection, diff/file context, resumable consultations, and parallel second opinions.
original_claim: Developers can request a second opinion from another AI CLI without leaving their current coding-agent session.
what_changed: Cross-model review is packaged as a lightweight reusable workflow instead of manual tool switching or custom orchestration.
why_it_matters: For architecture choices and uncertain agent decisions, deliberately consulting a different model can introduce structured disagreement and reduce single-model blind spots.
reason: Wildcard discovery with high practical value; the repository documents the workflow and was active on October 6.

source: Practitioner coverage citing OpenAI team announcement
author: Thibault Sottiaux
title: Codex Auto-review reportedly becomes free and off-plan for ChatGPT sign-ins
summary: Current practitioner coverage reports that Auto-review, which delegates eligible permission decisions to a second agent, is now free for ChatGPT-authenticated Codex users and does not draw from plan allowance.
original_claim: Auto-review is free for ChatGPT-authenticated Codex users and does not draw usage from the user's plan.
what_changed: The feature existed previously, but its marginal usage cost was reportedly removed on October 6.
why_it_matters: Permission prompts interrupt autonomous coding workflows; an off-plan reviewer agent could make longer Codex tasks substantially less interrupt-driven.
reason: High practical value, but the original announcement was not directly retrievable and written guidance may lag or conflict; Daily Curator should verify first-party documentation.

author: bujosa
title: Claude Code Channels used as a remote-supervision layer for long-running coding sessions
summary: A practitioner project demonstrates a concrete pattern for keeping a Claude Code session available on a host machine while using Anthropic's official Telegram Channel as the operator interface from a phone.
original_claim: The official Telegram Channel can be combined with a persistent host session to make long-running Claude Code work remotely supervisable.
what_changed: The useful signal is not the older Channels feature itself, but its packaging into a concrete long-running-agent operating pattern.
why_it_matters: Remote asynchronous supervision reduces the need to remain at the terminal while a coding agent works, while retaining the same repository and tool context.
reason: High-priority long-running-agent workflow. The official Channel mechanism is established; Daily Curator should validate the practitioner-specific persistence claims before promoting them to durable knowledge.
